question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,1).$ So, the $y$-intercept is $b=1.$ 

We can calculate the slope of the line by choosing two points on the line and applying the slope formula. The line passes through the points $(-4,2)$ and $(0,1),$ so we calculate its slope as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{1-2}{0-(-4)} \\  & =\frac{-1}{4} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=-\frac{1}{4}$ and the $y$-intercept $b=1$ into the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b,$ we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
y=-\frac{1}{4}x+1
$$
